title: The Pickwick Band and the Minatus brothers
summary: The Pickwick Band's two Minatus brothers led it; they lived across the river. A brief return to the blues.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: The Pickwood Band, he said.
Well, well, well. That's all right. That's all right. Pickwood, who was in that? What was that?
Who was in the Pickwood Band?
The two Minatus brothers.
The Minatus?
They used to live over the river.
Ask about the blues again, and we didn't get that. When he heard the blues?

Yeah, he said that, was he young when they played the blues? Yes. You just answered like you answered before. You say when they started to play the blues, was he a young man or you was already in age?
Oh, I was a pretty good child, yes.
They always did play the blues, huh?
Yeah, everybody was playing the blues.
Ask me if the Minatus were named Numb and Deuce.
The Minatus. Was they Numb and Deuce?
They threw two brothers. They was the first leader and the assistant leader. And they had another chopper, but I don't remember him.
They related to Manuel, I guess. Manuel.
Manuel Perez?
Manuel Mineta.
Manuel Mineta. You knew Emmanuel Mineta?
Emmanuel Mineta?
Yeah.
I didn't know his first name.
Where's the Mineta?
I know they both was Mineta. They live over the river. There's Boy and Grace over there.
